headline: SSR MINING SWALLOWS ROXMORE RESOURCES FOR $712M — CONVERSE GOLD IN NEVADA THE PRIZE
snippet: SSR Mining (TSX: SSRM) agreed to acquire Roxmore Resources and its Converse gold project in Nevada for a total deal value of $712 million, paying C$6.75 per share in cash plus shares in a spinout company — a 27% premium to Roxmore's October 9 closing price. Converse sits in the prolific Battle Mountain trend in Humboldt County, Nevada and provides SSR with a permitted, scalable open-pit gold development asset that diversifies away from its Çöpler mine in Turkey, which continues to operate under tailings management restrictions. The all-cash portion gives Roxmore shareholders certainty while the spinout preserves upside on non-core assets. No regulatory approvals beyond stock exchange consent are required; shareholders vote before year-end. For junior mining investors, the deal benchmarks Nevada gold development valuations at a 27% premium in the current cycle and confirms mid-tier producers are actively acquiring Tier 1 jurisdiction assets at today's gold prices.

headline: SKYLINE AND COVE KAZ MERGE TO FORM KAZ RESOURCES — KAZAKH TUNGSTEN ENTERS WESTERN CRITICAL METALS RADAR
snippet: Skyline Gold and Cove Kaz Resources signed a definitive merger agreement on October 14, with the combined company operating as Kaz Resources and focused on developing tungsten assets in Kazakhstan — a jurisdiction that supplies a meaningful share of global tungsten concentrate outside China. Tungsten is critical for cutting tools, armour-piercing munitions and high-performance alloys; China controls approximately 80% of global tungsten supply and has periodically restricted exports. A Western-aligned Kazakh tungsten development company adds an underrepresented critical mineral to the listed junior sector universe. The merger is targeted for completion during Q4 2026 or early Q1 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. Tungsten has received far less policy attention than lithium or rare earths to date, but its supply concentration and military-industrial demand profile make Kaz Resources a company worth tracking as Western governments broaden their critical minerals designation lists.

headline: GOLD FIELDS CIRCLES NORTHERN STAR — A$12.6B MEGA-MERGER WOULD CREATE TOP-FIVE GLOBAL GOLD PRODUCER
snippet: South Africa's Gold Fields has approached ASX-listed Northern Star Resources about a potential combination that would value the deal at approximately A$12.6 billion, according to reporting summarised by Forbes and Skillings.net, with Northern Star's management rejecting the initial approach. A completed deal would create one of the world's top-five gold producers by output, combining Gold Fields' African, Australian and Chilean assets with Northern Star's Tier 1 Australian operations including Kalgoorlie. Gold Fields previously acquired Osisko Mining in 2024, establishing a pattern of cross-border consolidation. Northern Star's rejection of the initial approach is typical deal choreography; the board faces the same pressure every major gold producer faces at current prices: turning down a premium scrip deal when the acquirer's currency is elevated is hard to justify without a credible standalone plan. The sector is watching whether Gold Fields returns with an improved bid or shifts attention elsewhere.

headline: MINING'S TOP 50 SHED $264B IN SEPTEMBER AS GOLD TRADE UNWINDS AND LITHIUM STOCKS EXIT
snippet: The world's 50 largest listed mining companies shed a combined $264 billion in market capitalisation during September 2026 as two major sector themes reversed simultaneously: gold's momentum trade unwound sharply from January records, and lithium equities continued their multi-month exit as spot spodumene prices fell approximately 25% over the past four weeks alone. Copper miners held up better in the rankings, as copper's structural demand story proved more resilient to macro rate-hike fears than either gold or battery metals. The September drawdown is the single largest monthly loss for the top 50 cohort in the current cycle, reflecting how much positioning had built into gold and how deep the re-rating of lithium development assets continues to run. The report also noted that Rio Tinto rejected speculation of merger talks with Glencore, clearing one of the market's outstanding M&A question marks. For junior mining investors tracking the asset allocation cycle, the divergence between copper's relative resilience and gold/lithium's simultaneous September correction is a meaningful regime signal.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM BACK ONLINE IN BRAZIL AFTER COURT LIFTS EMERGENCY HALT ON GROTA DO CIRILO
snippet: A Brazilian federal appeals court lifted the emergency injunction that had halted production at Sigma Lithium's Grota do Cirilo operation in Minas Gerais on approximately October 15, allowing the company to restart Brazil's largest operating hard-rock lithium mine. The September emergency order had been sought by an environmental group challenging the mine's licensing and had removed approximately 55,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent of annual capacity from Brazil's output. The restart is a relief for Sigma shareholders following a quarter marked by the production halt, falling spot lithium prices and broader sector selling. Brazil has positioned itself as a strategic Western-aligned lithium supplier; the court's decision removes a near-term political risk that had begun to raise questions about operational predictability in the country's mining regulatory framework. Sigma Lithium's ability to resume operations quickly after the injunction was lifted demonstrates the resilience of the licensing basis underpinning Grota do Cirilo.

headline: USA RARE EARTH CLIMBS 4% AS MONTH-LONG SELLOFF PAUSES — STABILIZATION OR DEAD-CAT BOUNCE?
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) climbed 4% on October 15 as a month-long sector correction in domestic rare earth and critical mineral equities showed signs of exhaustion, with MP Materials ticking modestly higher and United States Antimony dipping slightly in the mixed session. The selloff had been driven by improving US-China trade relations reducing the perceived urgency of domestic rare earth supply chain buildout — a thesis headwind when geopolitical premium is the primary valuation driver. Analysts tracking the sector note the bounce arrived on light volume with no company-specific catalyst, raising the question of whether it represents genuine accumulation or a temporary relief rally ahead of the November 10 China rare earth export control expiry date. USA Rare Earth's pending $2.8 billion acquisition of Brazil's Serra Verde Group remains a live event-driven catalyst that could reframe the stock's narrative if the deal closes as expected. The bounce was uneven across the sector, underscoring that name selection within domestic rare earths matters more than sector-level positioning right now.

headline: TRUMP'S GREENLAND MINERAL PUSH LIFTS CRITICAL METALS 4% — TANBREEZ RARE EARTH ONSHORE RIGHTS UNAFFECTED BY SEABED BAN
snippet: Critical Metals (Nasdaq: CRML) shares rose approximately 4% on October 14 after President Trump announced that 'massive exploration for oil, gas and minerals is preparing to begin' in Greenland, directly benefiting CRML's Tanbreez rare earth project — the world's largest identified rare earth deposit by ionic abundance. On the same day, USA Rare Earth fell 3% and MP Materials slipped 2%, illustrating the selective rather than sector-wide nature of the Trump news. Greenland's parliament subsequently voted unanimously to ban seabed mineral extraction, a move the market interpreted as targeted at offshore projects rather than Tanbreez's onshore mineral rights. The net read for Tanbreez investors: the Trump announcement raised the political profile of Greenland's rare earth potential, and Greenland's autonomous government simultaneously signalled it will maintain sovereign control over the terms of development — making political relationship management between Ottawa, Washington and Nuuk the key non-geological risk for the project.

headline: MINK VENTURES HITS COPPER-NICKEL-COBALT RAK ZONE AT RANKIN, MANITOBA — MULTI-METAL ASSAYS IN THOMPSON BELT
snippet: Mink Ventures (TSX-V: MINK) announced laboratory-confirmed assays from a new copper-nickel-cobalt zone at its Rankin property in Manitoba on October 15, reporting the RAK Zone grading 0.5745% Ni, 0.8798% Cu and 0.0756% Co over 2.1 metres. While the initial intercept is narrow, the multi-metal nature of the discovery — combining three critical metals in a single mineralized zone — is notable for a junior at the drill-targeting stage. Rankin sits within the Thompson Nickel Belt, one of Canada's premier established nickel corridors and home to Vale's Thompson mine and Exiro's recently acquired complex. The Thompson Belt context adds geological credibility to the RAK Zone and increases the probability of system-scale extensions at depth or along strike. The company will need wider widths or grade improvements to define a mineable resource, but the discovery of a new multi-metal zone in a proven producing belt is the kind of initial step that can anchor a multi-year drill programme.

headline: CANUC RESOURCES FINDS GOLD BESIDE A DECADES-OLD PIT IN SUDBURY — NEAR-SURFACE DISCOVERY LIFTS SHARES
snippet: Canuc Resources (TSX-V: CDA) announced a new near-surface gold zone at its East Sudbury Project in Ontario, located directly adjacent to a past-producing open pit, with shares rising meaningfully on the discovery announcement. The Sudbury Basin is world-class for nickel-copper-PGM geology, but a gold zone beside historical workings adds precious metals optionality to a jurisdiction where existing infrastructure, roads, power and metallurgical expertise significantly reduce development costs compared with remote greenfield properties. Near-surface gold beside past-producing pits carries inherently lower exploration risk: prior mining proves economic concentrations existed in the system, and the discovery geometry is substantially easier to model than a blind greenfield target. Initial grade and width details were not disclosed in the announcement; follow-on drilling results will define the zone's dimensions and economics and are the key catalysts to track. Small-cap TSX-V gold discoveries in established mining camps with proven infrastructure are exactly the type of early-stage story this site's research framework is designed to evaluate.

headline: HOCHSCHILD HOLDS FULL-YEAR GUIDANCE — PERU AND ARGENTINA SILVER-GOLD MARGINS INTACT DESPITE RISING AISC
snippet: Hochschild Mining (LSE: HOC) confirmed its full-year production and cost guidance in a recent Q3 operational update, citing strong gold and silver prices as the margin buffer against rising all-in sustaining costs at its San Jose operation in Argentina and Inmaculada operation in Peru. The London-listed silver-gold mid-tier producer has guided for approximately 375,000-385,000 gold equivalent ounces for the year. With silver holding above $57 per ounce and gold near $4,165, Hochschild's revenue per ounce sold is running substantially above management's internal planning assumptions, providing a meaningful financial cushion against the labour cost inflation and community engagement expenditures that continue to pressure South American mining operating expenses in the current cycle. The guidance hold is a signal of operational stability at a time when several Latin American peers have been forced to revise forecasts downward due to regulatory complications, permitting delays and geological issues — Hochschild's ability to maintain guidance is a competitive differentiator in the peer group.

headline: ARGONAUT ANALYST: LITHIUM AND COPPER THEMATIC UNCHANGED DESPITE 25% PRICE CRASH — LONG-TERM DEMAND STILL THERE
snippet: An Argonaut analyst told Stockhead that the long-term investment case for lithium and copper remains structurally intact despite spot prices for lithium carbonate and spodumene falling approximately 25% over the past month and copper retreating from near-record LME levels. The analyst's argument rests on demand certainty versus supply response uncertainty: EV adoption curves and grid infrastructure investment are policy-mandated at government level and are not discretionary, while the mines needed to supply that long-term demand cannot be built fast enough regardless of current spot prices — permitting timelines, capital access and jurisdictional risk ensure a structural supply gap opens in the early 2030s. The 'nothing changes the ultimate thematic' framing is a direct counter to the sector rotation thesis driving retail flows out of battery metals and into gold producers. For ASX and TSX-V lithium developers still holding cash and a defined project, the message is that asset values have not permanently de-rated — only the market's short-term patience has thinned. Junior investors with a 3-5 year time horizon should distinguish between commodity price volatility and the underlying demand case.
